name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Chemical nature of major plant growth regulators

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical classes of plant growth regulators in Column I with their representative compounds or precursors in Column II:

Column I (Chemical Class) Column II (Representative Compound)
A. Indole compounds I. Abscisic acid (ABA)
B. Adenine derivatives II. Gibberellic acid (\(\text{GA}_3\))
C. Carotenoid derivatives III. Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA)
D. Terpenes IV. \(N^6\)-furfurylamino purine (kinetin)

Select the correct match from the options below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify indole compounds.
Plant growth regulators derived from indole rings include indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and indole butyric acid (IBA). Hence, indole compounds correspond to indole-3-acetic acid (IAA).

Step 2: Identify adenine derivatives.
Cytokinins are purine derivatives; specifically, kinetin is chemically \(N^6\)-furfurylamino purine, an adenine derivative. Hence, adenine derivatives correspond to \(N^6\)-furfurylamino purine (kinetin).

Step 3: Identify carotenoid derivatives.
Abscisic acid (ABA) is biochemically synthesised as a derivative of carotenoids. Hence, carotenoid derivatives correspond to abscisic acid (ABA).

Step 4: Identify terpenes.
Gibberellins, such as \(\text{GA}_3\), are diterpenoid acids synthesized from terpene pathways. Hence, terpenes correspond to gibberellic acid (\(\text{GA}_3\)).

Step 5: Formulate the complete matching set.
Combining the established individual associations yields: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Discovery and isolation of plant growth regulators

questiontext.text:
Match the scientists in Column I with their pioneering observations or isolations in Column II:

Column I (Scientist / Discoverer) Column II (Key Contribution)
A. Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin I. Isolated auxin from coleoptile tips of oat seedlings
B. E. Kurosawa II. Confirmed volatile substance from ripened oranges hastening fruit ripening
C. F.W. Went III. Demonstrated phototropic bending at the coleoptile tip in canary grass
D. H.H. Cousins IV. Discovered bakanae disease symptoms using sterile fungal filtrates

Choose the correct matching sequence:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the contribution of Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin.
Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass bent towards unilateral light, proving the coleoptile tip was the source of a transmittable influence. Hence, Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin match with demonstrating phototropic bending at the coleoptile tip in canary grass.

Step 2: Identify the contribution of E. Kurosawa.
E. Kurosawa (1926) treated uninfected rice seedlings with sterile filtrates of the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi and observed bakanae (foolish seedling) disease symptoms. Hence, E. Kurosawa matches with discovering bakanae disease symptoms using sterile fungal filtrates.

Step 3: Identify the contribution of F.W. Went.
F.W. Went successfully isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of Avena (oat) seedlings using agar blocks. Hence, F.W. Went matches with isolating auxin from coleoptile tips of oat seedlings.

Step 4: Identify the contribution of H.H. Cousins.
H.H. Cousins (1910) demonstrated that a volatile substance emitted from ripened oranges accelerated ripening of unripened bananas, which was later identified as ethylene. Hence, H.H. Cousins matches with confirming volatile substance from ripened oranges hastening fruit ripening.

Step 5: Formulate the complete matching set.
The correct overall combination is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Parameters used to measure plant growth

questiontext.text:
Match the plant structures or organs listed in Column I with the specific parameter typically employed to quantify their growth in Column II:

Column I (Organ / Cell Type) Column II (Growth Parameter)
A. Single maize root apical meristem I. Increase in length
B. Watermelon fruit cell II. Increase in surface area
C. Pollen tube III. Increase in cell number
D. Dorsiventral leaf IV. Increase in cell volume or size

Identify the correct set of pairings:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate growth in maize root apical meristem.
A single maize root apical meristem can produce more than 17,500 new cells per hour; here, growth is measured as an increase in cell number.

Step 2: Evaluate growth in watermelon cells.
Cells in a watermelon may expand up to 3,50,000 times their original size; here, growth is measured as an increase in cell volume or size.

Step 3: Evaluate growth in a pollen tube.
The elongation of a pollen tube during its passage through the style is direct longitudinal extension; thus, its growth is measured in terms of length.

Step 4: Evaluate growth in a dorsiventral leaf.
A developing dorsiventral leaf expands planar lamina tissue; therefore, its growth is measured in terms of surface area.

Step 5: Formulate the final match.
The resulting pairings are A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Cellular characteristics across plant growth phases

questiontext.text:
Match the phases of cellular growth in Column I with their primary cellular characteristics in Column II:

Column I (Phase of Growth) Column II (Cellular Characteristics)
A. Meristematic phase I. Attainment of maximal size, wall thickening, and protoplasmic modifications
B. Elongation phase II. Rich in protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary walls with abundant plasmodesmata
C. Maturation phase III. Increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition
D. Senescence phase IV. Progressive metabolic decline and structural deterioration terminating in death

Select the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the meristematic phase.
Cells at the growing apices represent the meristematic phase. They are densely cytoplasmic, possess prominent nuclei, and have thin primary cellulosic walls with abundant plasmodesmata. Thus, the meristematic phase matches with rich in protoplasm, large conspicuous nuclei, thin primary walls with abundant plasmodesmata.

Step 2: Analyze the elongation phase.
Cells proximal to the meristematic zone undergo the elongation phase, characterized by extensive cell enlargement, development of large central vacuoles, and synthesis/deposition of new wall materials. Thus, the elongation phase matches with increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition.

Step 3: Analyze the maturation phase.
More proximal cells undergo differentiation and maturation, achieving their maximal dimensions, secondary wall thickenings (such as lignification in tracheary elements), and specific protoplasmic adaptations. Thus, the maturation phase matches with attainment of maximal size, wall thickening, and protoplasmic modifications.

Step 4: Analyze the senescence phase.
Senescence represents the terminal developmental phase characterized by irreversible functional loss and degradation leading directly to cellular or organ death. Thus, senescence matches with progressive metabolic decline and structural deterioration terminating in death.

Step 5: Formulate the full matching sequence.
The correct association is A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Horticultural applications of auxins and gibberellins

questiontext.text:
Match the agricultural/horticultural treatments in Column I with their corresponding effects or active agents in Column II:

Column I (Application or Technique) Column II (Direct Response / Phytohormone Involved)
A. 2, 4-D spray on lawns I. Speeds up the malting process in the brewing industry
B. Shoot tip decapitation in tea plantations II. Selective eradication of broad-leaved dicotyledonous weeds
C. Gibberellin treatment on sugarcane crop III. Overcomes apical dominance to induce vigorous lateral bud outgrowth
D. Application of \(\text{GA}_3\) in barley grains IV. Elongates stem internodes, increasing yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre

Choose the correct combination from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze 2, 4-D spray.
2, 4-D (2, 4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) is a synthetic auxin extensively used as a selective herbicide to destroy broad-leaved dicot weeds without harming mature monocotyledonous grasses. Hence, 2, 4-D matches with selective eradication of broad-leaved dicotyledonous weeds.

Step 2: Analyze shoot tip decapitation.
In tea gardens and hedge-making, decapitation (removal of the shoot apex) eliminates the primary source of auxin, relieving lateral axillary buds from apical dominance and promoting dense branching. Hence, decapitation matches with overcomes apical dominance to induce vigorous lateral bud outgrowth.

Step 3: Analyze gibberellin spray on sugarcane.
Sugarcane stores sucrose in its stem internodes. Exogenous application of gibberellins lengthens the stems, boosting total yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre. Hence, gibberellin on sugarcane matches with elongates stem internodes, increasing yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre.

Step 4: Analyze \(\text{GA}_3\) application in barley grains.
\(\text{GA}_3\) stimulates the synthesis of \(\alpha\)-amylase and other hydrolytic enzymes in the aleurone layer of germinating grains, significantly accelerating the malting process in brewing. Hence, \(\text{GA}_3\) in barley matches with speeds up the malting process in the brewing industry.

Step 5: Synthesize the full set of pairings.
The correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Physiological actions and applications of ethylene

questiontext.text:
Match the physiological responses or applications of ethylene in Column I with their detailed descriptions in Column II:

Column I (Phenomenon / Application) Column II (Physiological Manifestation)
A. Respiratory climacteric I. Promotes rapid petiole and internode elongation keeping shoot parts above water
B. Deep-water rice response II. Dramatic increase in respiration rate during fruit ripening
C. Ethephon spray on orchards III. Induces horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of axis, and apical hook formation
D. Triple response of dicot seedlings IV. Accelerates abscission and fruit thinning in cotton, cherry, and walnut

Identify the correct matching option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define respiratory climacteric.
During the ripening of many fleshy fruits (e.g., apples, bananas, tomatoes), ethylene stimulates a steep, transient upsurge in cellular respiration known as the respiratory climacteric. Thus, respiratory climacteric corresponds to dramatic increase in respiration rate during fruit ripening.

Step 2: Define deep-water rice response.
In submerged deep-water rice fields, accumulated ethylene promotes rapid internode and petiole elongation, allowing upper photosynthetic foliage to stay above the rising water level. Thus, deep-water rice response corresponds to promotes rapid petiole and internode elongation keeping shoot parts above water.

Step 3: Define commercial ethephon action.
Ethephon releases ethylene inside plant tissues, promoting fruit ripening and hastening abscission of floral and young fruit organs; this effect is exploited commercially for thinning walnut, cherry, and cotton crops. Thus, ethephon spray corresponds to accelerates abscission and fruit thinning in cotton, cherry, and walnut.

Step 4: Define the classic triple response of dicot seedlings.
Under ethylene exposure, germinating dicot seedlings exhibit three morphological changes: horizontal growth, radial swelling of the hypocotyl/axis, and exaggerated curvature of the apical hook. Thus, triple response corresponds to induces horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of axis, and apical hook formation.

Step 5: Formulate the complete matching sequence.
The correct matching sequence is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Types of developmental plasticity and heterophylly

questiontext.text:
Match the plant species or conditions in Column I with the corresponding manifestation of developmental plasticity in Column II:

Column I (Plant / Condition) Column II (Form of Plasticity / Feature)
A. Cotton and coriander I. Intrinsic phase-dependent heterophylly in juvenile versus adult leaves
B. Buttercup (Ranunculus) II. Developmental heterophylly controlled by internal life-cycle phases
C. Larkspur III. Environmental heterophylly between terrestrial and aquatic habitats
D. Submerged aquatic leaves of buttercup IV. Finely dissected, filamentous segments adapted to water currents

Which of the following represents the correct match?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand heterophylly in cotton and coriander.
In cotton and coriander, heterophylly represents an intrinsic programmed developmental change where the shape of leaves formed during the juvenile phase differs from that of leaves on the mature adult plant. Hence, cotton and coriander match with developmental heterophylly controlled by internal life-cycle phases.

Step 2: Understand heterophylly in buttercup.
Buttercup demonstrates environmental plasticity (environmental heterophylly), producing broad, lobed leaves in air and finely dissected leaves when submerged in water. Hence, buttercup matches with environmental heterophylly between terrestrial and aquatic habitats.

Step 3: Understand heterophylly in larkspur.
Larkspur shows distinct leaf morphology along its developmental axis, where juvenile leaves have simpler outlines and adult leaves become deeply incised and lobed due to life-phase progression. Hence, larkspur matches with intrinsic phase-dependent heterophylly in juvenile versus adult leaves.

Step 4: Understand the structure of submerged buttercup leaves.
The submerged foliage of buttercup develops as highly dissected, ribbon-like or filiform segments that minimize resistance to flowing water currents and maximize gas diffusion underwater. Hence, submerged aquatic leaves of buttercup match with finely dissected, filamentous segments adapted to water currents.

Step 5: Formulate the final matching sequence.
The correct match is A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Cellular differentiation dedifferentiation and redifferentiation processes

questiontext.text:
Match the tissue development events in Column I with the biological differentiation phenomenon in Column II:

Column I (Developmental Event) Column II (Cellular Phenomenon)
A. Tracheary element formation from procambium I. Redifferentiation of secondary meristem derivatives
B. Formation of interfascicular cambium from medullary rays II. Positional / open differentiation relative to meristem location
C. Formation of secondary cortex (phelloderm) from cork cambium III. Primary differentiation involving protoplasmic loss and lignification
D. Epidermal cell formation at the root periphery versus root cap cells at the apex IV. Dedifferentiation of fully mature parenchymatous cells

Select the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze tracheary element formation.
Cells derived from primary meristems mature into tracheary elements by losing their living protoplasm and developing robust, lignocellulosic secondary walls to conduct water under tension; this is primary differentiation. Hence, tracheary element formation corresponds to primary differentiation involving protoplasmic loss and lignification.

Step 2: Analyze interfascicular cambium formation.
Living, fully differentiated parenchyma cells of the medullary rays regain the capacity to divide mitotically, forming interfascicular cambium; this phenomenon of regaining division capacity is dedifferentiation. Hence, interfascicular cambium formation corresponds to dedifferentiation of fully mature parenchymatous cells.

Step 3: Analyze secondary cortex (phelloderm) formation.
The cells cut off by the cork cambium (a secondary lateral meristem) subsequently lose their division ability again and mature into specialized tissues such as phelloderm; this second round of specialization is redifferentiation. Hence, secondary cortex formation corresponds to redifferentiation of secondary meristem derivatives.

Step 4: Analyze peripheral versus apical fate of root meristem derivatives.
Derivatives pushed to the exterior differentiate into epidermis, whereas cells pushed downward away from the apex form the protective root cap; this demonstrates open differentiation determined by positional cues. Hence, epidermal versus root cap differentiation corresponds to positional / open differentiation relative to meristem location.

Step 5: Formulate the full matching sequence.
The correct sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Mathematical expressions and models of growth rates

questiontext.text:
Match the mathematical equations and kinetic concepts in Column I with their correct biological descriptions in Column II:

Column I (Equation / Concept) Column II (Biological Significance)
A. \(L_t = L_0 + rt\) I. Efficiency index representing the capacity to generate new plant biomass
B. \(W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}\) II. Sigmoidal growth pattern of cells and organs under natural nutrient limitations
C. Relative growth rate (\(r\)) III. Arithmetic constant linear growth where only one progeny continues to divide
D. Sigmoid curve IV. Geometric growth where all daughter cells retain mitotic ability

Choose the correct matching:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate arithmetic growth.
In arithmetic growth, only one daughter cell continues dividing while the other differentiates, producing a straight line on a plot of length against time described by the equation \(L_t = L_0 + rt\). Thus, \(L_t = L_0 + rt\) corresponds to arithmetic constant linear growth where only one progeny continues to divide.

Step 2: Evaluate geometric exponential growth.
In geometric growth, both daughter cells retain dividing ability, leading to an exponential increase in size/biomass expressed as \(W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}\). Thus, \(W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}\) corresponds to geometric growth where all daughter cells retain mitotic ability.

Step 3: Evaluate relative growth rate (\(r\)).
In the geometric equation, \(r\) denotes the relative growth rate and serves as a quantitative measure of the plant's capacity to synthesize new biomass per unit initial parameter, termed the efficiency index. Thus, relative growth rate corresponds to efficiency index representing the capacity to generate new plant biomass.

Step 4: Evaluate the sigmoid curve.
Under natural conditions, exponential growth cannot be sustained infinitely because nutrient and environmental resources become limiting, transitioning from lag to log, and finally to a stationary phase. Thus, the sigmoid curve corresponds to sigmoidal growth pattern of cells and organs under natural nutrient limitations.

Step 5: Formulate the matching set.
The correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANT_GROWTH_AND_DEVELOPMENT_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Quantitative growth rates and regulatory hormone interactions

questiontext.text:
Match the comparative growth parameters or hormone actions in Column I with their quantitative values or regulators in Column II:

Column I (Parameter / Action) Column II (Quantitative Value / Phytohormone)
A. Relative growth rate of Leaf A (expanding from \(5\text{ cm}^2\) to \(10\text{ cm}^2\)) I. \(0.10\) or \(10\%\) per unit time
B. Relative growth rate of Leaf B (expanding from \(50\text{ cm}^2\) to \(55\text{ cm}^2\)) II. \(1.00\) or \(100\%\) per unit time
C. Antagonist to gibberellins regarding seed dormancy III. Cytokinin
D. Phytohormone promoting nutrient mobilisation to delay senescence IV. Abscisic acid (ABA)

Select the correct match:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Calculate the relative growth rate of Leaf A.
Leaf A starts with an initial area of \(5\text{ cm}^2\) and gains \(5\text{ cm}^2\) to become \(10\text{ cm}^2\). Its relative growth rate is \(\frac{\text{Growth}}{\text{Initial Parameter}} = \frac{5\text{ cm}^2}{5\text{ cm}^2} = 1.00\) or \(100\%\) per unit time. Thus, Leaf A corresponds to \(1.00\) or \(100\%\) per unit time.

Step 2: Calculate the relative growth rate of Leaf B.
Leaf B starts with an initial area of \(50\text{ cm}^2\) and gains \(5\text{ cm}^2\) to become \(55\text{ cm}^2\). Its relative growth rate is \(\frac{\text{Growth}}{\text{Initial Parameter}} = \frac{5\text{ cm}^2}{50\text{ cm}^2} = 0.10\) or \(10\%\) per unit time. Thus, Leaf B corresponds to \(0.10\) or \(10\%\) per unit time.

Step 3: Identify the antagonist to gibberellins in seed dormancy.
While gibberellins promote seed germination and break dormancy by inducing hydrolytic enzymes, abscisic acid (ABA) induces and maintains dormancy, enabling seeds to withstand desiccation; thus, ABA acts as a key antagonist to GAs. Hence, the antagonist to gibberellins matches with abscisic acid (ABA).

Step 4: Identify the hormone promoting nutrient mobilisation to delay senescence.
Cytokinins mobilize nutrients toward mature organs, which prevents premature chlorophyll breakdown and significantly delays leaf senescence (the Richmond-Lang effect). Hence, the hormone delaying leaf senescence matches with cytokinin.

Step 5: Formulate the full matching sequence.
The correct match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.
